skills_to_grow: Watch the pass when the sanitation list is blank

role.ambitious_version: She still corrects, teaches, runs the pass and orders. A blank par stays blank until she names the quantity, and a line she rejects is hers to drop.

tasks.short: Monitor sanitation practices on the kitchen walk.

steps.what: List the stored sanitation standards for this service.
Notice whether employees follow those sanitation practices.
Record the sanitation result she observed on the walk.
Tell a cook to correct the sanitation lapse.

tasks.design: {DOCS} lists the stored sanitation checks for this service before she walks the kitchen. She still notices whether employees follow them, records the result she saw, and tells a cook to correct a lapse. The list does not fill the log, does not raise an alert, and does not send the record.
tasks.previous_blocker: The sanitation checks sat on a posted sheet she had to find before the walk.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can list the stored checks for this service before she walks. The walk and the correction are still hers.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see whether employees follow the practices. A list cannot see a lapse.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can tell a cook to correct what she just saw.
tasks.altitude: She still walks, records and corrects. She stops hunting the posted checks. She does not gain a right to let the list write the log or correct a cook.

reach.task: Follow the sanitation correction she gave.
reach.learn: Which checks the list already names, so a blank list is not treated as a known standard.

evidence.claim: A food business needs a HACCP plan. The NVWA-approved Hygiënecode voor de horeca can meet it, and inspectors check the records unannounced. She still writes the result she saw. The list only shows the stored checks.
Hygiene-code records are kept six months, and one year for unchilled display. This design does not delete the log.

Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, WOR art. 27(1)(k) and (l) give consent rights on staff data and on systems fit to monitor attendance, behaviour or performance. This list is station checks. It does not score a named cook and it does not record attendance.
Annex III 4(b) covers task allocation by individual behaviour or traits and performance monitoring. This list does not rank cooks and does not allocate shifts.
The range is a scenario for a walk she still has to make. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The check list has site, check name, and what clean means. The producer is whoever keeps the hygiene-code list, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the site is blank or the list names the wrong site, the list step does not run. She monitors from the posted code, and the walk stays at full time. A blank is not filled with a guess.
The log line (check name, what she saw, the time) is produced by her when she records the result. That step stays at full time.
Noticing the practices and telling the cook stay at full time. The only shortened step is listing checks that are already stored.
The list does not fill the log, does not raise an alert, and does not send the record. It is equipment and station text. It does not score a cook and it does not record attendance.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when the list names the wrong site. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether the inspector expects a named person on each log line.
Whether this kitchen keeps the checks as a stored list, or only on the posted code.
research_questions: On a week of walks, how often is the sanitation list filled for that service before she starts?
How often do the stored checks disagree with the posted code?

incremental.description: Tell the office when the stored sanitation list names the wrong site. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the site and the check names are already stored, she skips hunting the posted sheet. When the list is blank or names the wrong site, she monitors from the posted code and the saving is zero. Noticing the practices, recording the result, and telling the cook are not shortened.

tasks.short: Instruct cooks on preparation and presentation.

steps.what: Read the dish named for this preparation.
List the stored cooking and garnishing method for that dish.
Instruct cooks on preparation, cooking, garnishing and presentation.

tasks.design: She reads the dish on the ticket first. {DOCS} then lists the stored cooking, garnishing, presentation and allergen names for that dish, and she still instructs the cooks herself. The list does not instruct, does not speak to a guest, and does not send a message.
tasks.previous_blocker: The method sat in a book she had to open while the cooks waited.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can list the stored method for the dish she just read. She still instructs the cooks.
tasks.still_hard: The cooks need her voice on preparation and presentation. A card does not instruct.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can instruct the cooks on this dish at this pass.
tasks.altitude: She still reads the ticket and still instructs. She stops hunting a method that is already on file. She does not gain a right to let the card teach the line or speak to a guest.

reach.learn: Which garnish the card already names, so a blank card is not treated as a known method.

evidence.claim: Guests must get information on the 14 EU allergens. The card shows the stored allergen names. She still instructs the cook. The card does not speak to the guest.

In 2022 only 41% of inspected horeca complied with allergen-information rules, often because the information was not available in writing or electronically. The card is a written list for the cook she instructs. The figure is an inspection result, not this kitchen's rate and not a time saving.
The range is a scenario for an instruction she still gives at the pass. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The order ticket is written by the waiter or the pass before this task. She reads the dish name from it in the first step, at full time. That read is counted here.

The method card has dish name, method steps, garnish note, presentation note, and allergen names. The producer is whoever keeps the recipe file, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the dish name is blank, or the card has no method for that dish, the list step does not run and does not invent steps. She instructs from the book, and that time stays full.
Instructing the cooks stays at full time. The only shortened step is listing a method that is already stored.
The list does not instruct, does not speak to a guest, and does not send a message.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when the card is for the wrong dish. That telling is her own speech. The list does not send it.
unknowns: Whether the recipe file already stores the 14 allergen names on each dish.
Whether tickets at this pass name the dish in words she can match to the recipe file.
research_questions: On a service, how often does a ticket dish have no stored method?
How often is the allergen list on the card missing one of the 14 names the rule requires?

incremental.description: Tell the office when the stored method card is for the wrong dish. The list does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the dish she read already has a stored method, she skips hunting the book. When the card is blank or the dish is missing, she instructs from the book and the saving is zero. Reading the ticket and instructing the cooks are not shortened.

steps.what: List the stored station plan for this preparation service.
Notice which preparation activities are behind.
Decide the next call for those preparation activities.
Supervise cooks on the food preparation she just called.

tasks.design: {DOCS} lists the stored station plan for this service before the first call. She still notices which activities are behind, decides the next call, and supervises the cooks. The plan does not name a cook, does not raise an alert, and does not send a ticket.
tasks.previous_blocker: The station plan sat on a board she had to read while the line was already moving.
tasks.enabler_now: A document store can list the stored station plan before the first call. She still notices, decides and supervises.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to see which activities are behind and call the next one.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can decide the next call and supervise the cooks.
tasks.altitude: She still notices, decides and calls the pass. She stops hunting a station plan that is already filed. She does not gain a right to let the plan assign a cook.

reach.learn: Which station the plan already names, so a blank plan is not treated as a known station.

evidence.claim: Where the Dutch works-council rule applies, WOR art. 27(1)(l) gives consent rights on systems fit to monitor attendance, behaviour or performance. This plan is dishes and stations. It does not monitor attendance.
Annex III 4(b) covers task allocation by individual behaviour or traits and performance monitoring. This plan does not allocate shifts by behaviour and does not rank cooks.
GDPR art. 22 bars a decision based solely on automated processing that has a significant effect, save exceptions with safeguards. She decides the next call. The plan does not assign a cook.
The range is a scenario for a pass she still calls. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The service name is the service she is already running. The station plan has course or dish, and station name. It has no cook name and no shift. The producer is whoever filed the plan, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
If the plan is blank, the list step does not run. She calls the pass from the board she already knows, and that time stays full.
Noticing which activities are behind, deciding the next call, and supervising the cooks stay at full time. The only shortened step is listing a plan that is already stored.
The plan does not name a cook, does not raise an alert, and does not send a ticket. She does not gain a right to let the plan assign a person.
Upkeep is 0.2 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for telling the office when a station name is wrong. That telling is her own speech. The plan does not send it.
unknowns: Whether the station plan is written down or only in her head.
Whether this workplace is covered by the Dutch works-council rule.
research_questions: On a week of services, how often is a station plan filed before the first call?
How often does the plan name a station that is closed that day?

incremental.description: Tell the office when a stored station name is wrong. The plan does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When the station plan is already stored for this service, she skips hunting the board. When the plan is blank, she calls the pass from the board she knows and the saving is zero. Noticing the line, deciding the next call, and supervising the cooks are not shortened.

tasks.short: Order food and other supplies for the kitchen.

steps.what: List stored par levels for the food supplies.
Record the count of food and supplies on hand.
Draft food order lines from the par levels and her count.
Check the draft still matches the food service she will run.
Order the food and supplies she accepted from the supplier.

tasks.design: She records the count first. The {SPREADSHEET} lists the stored par levels and drafts order lines from those levels, her count and the stored pack price, and she checks the lines against the service before she places the order. The draft writes those order lines, does not raise an alert, and does not send the order.
tasks.previous_blocker: Par levels sat in a book, and the order lines were written by hand after the count.
tasks.enabler_now: A spreadsheet can list the stored par levels and draft order lines from her count. She still counts, checks and places the order.
tasks.still_hard: She still has to count what is on hand and phone the supplier. The draft does not place the order.
tasks.human_edge: Only she can accept the quantity for the service she will run and place the order.
tasks.altitude: She still counts, checks and phones the supplier. She stops hunting the par book and writing the same lines by hand. She does not gain a right to let the draft send the order.

reach.task: Use the food once it arrives.
reach.learn: Which lines she already ordered, so a blank par is not treated as an ordered item.

evidence.claim: Apicbase rolls ingredient prices up to portion cost, applies connected suppliers' price changes and adds labour for a prime cost. The draft only copies a stored pack price onto an order line. She still counts, checks the quantity and places the order. The source is recipe costing, not a measured saving, and it is not claimed to send a purchase order.
The range is a scenario for an order whose par levels are already stored. It is not a published time study. Model knowledge.

assumptions: The par card has item name, par quantity, unit and pack price. The producer is whoever keeps the par book, before this task. That capture is outside this task and is not counted as time saved.
The count sheet has item name, quantity on hand and unit. She produces it when she records the count, at full time. The draft uses that count. It does not invent a quantity.

If the par card is blank or the count sheet is blank, the draft step does not run. She orders from the stores, and that time stays full. If the pack price is blank, the price cell stays empty and the quantity line can still be drafted.
Counting, checking the lines against the service, and phoning the supplier stay at full time. The shortened steps are listing the stored par levels and drafting the order lines.
The draft writes the order lines and nothing else. It does not raise an alert, does not send the order, and does not post it to a ledger. She places the order by phone.
The check of quantities against the service sits in that review and is not counted again as new work.
Upkeep is 0.3 hours per 100 baseline hours of this task, for correcting a stale par or pack price before she orders. The draft does not send that correction.
unknowns: Whether pack prices are already on the par book or only on the supplier's site.
Who at this kitchen may order above the par, and for which service.
research_questions: On the last ten orders, how often were par quantity and pack price filled before she counted?
How often did the quantity she accepted differ from par minus the count?

already_counted.description: Check the drafted lines cover the food service she will run, not only that par minus the count subtracts. The time sits in that review.

incremental.description: Correct a stale par or pack price before she orders. The draft does not send that correction.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: When par levels are already stored and she has recorded the count, the draft writes the order lines and she skips writing them by hand. When the par or the count is blank, the draft does not run and she orders from the stores, so the saving is zero. Counting, checking the service, and phoning the supplier are not shortened.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional
